title: Caching, Cost, and Token Management
description: Control AI backend costs with caching, batching, token budgets, and provider-aware budgeting in C#.

blocks.text: AI backends can become expensive without limits. Caching, batching, token budgets, and fallback policies keep costs predictable while preserving user experience.

blocks.title: Practical cost controls
items: **Response caching** — cache answers for common questions with stable context.
**Retrieval caching** — cache retrieved chunks for repeated or similar queries.
**Token budgets** — limit prompt and completion tokens per request.
**Batching** — process embedding and generation jobs in batches.
**Fallback models** — use cheaper models for simpler requests when possible.

blocks.title: Conceptual token-budget guard
blocks.content: Enforce token limits before sending requests to the model.

blocks.title: Cache invalidation is hard
blocks.text: Cache embeddings and retrieval results carefully. If source documents change, invalidate related caches before serving stale context.

items.text: I can estimate the cost of a RAG request
items.hint: Sum embedding, retrieval, prompt, and completion costs

items.text: I know when caching is safe versus risky
items.hint: Cache stable content; invalidate when documents or prompts change

items.text: I can enforce a token budget in code
items.hint: Check before sending and limit output tokens with provider options

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Cost control starts with observability and limits.
Cache retrieval and responses where user experience allows.
Token budgets prevent runaway prompts and surprise bills.
blocks.takeaway: Design cost controls into the pipeline, not around it. Budgets and caches should be first-class components.
